summary: Moves RFC 3525, Gateway Control Protocol Version 1, to Historic status and obsoletes it. It is an informational memo.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo reclassifies RFC 3525 as Historic because the ITU-T continued developing the same protocol as H.248.1. It explains why the older RFC no longer describes the protocol as it was standardized at the time.

subtitle: RFC 3525 moves to Historic as ITU-T continued developing H.248.1.

tldr.problem: RFC 3525 no longer reflected the evolving Megaco/H.248 protocol after the ITU-T took ownership and published later versions.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5125 obsoletes RFC 3525 and reclassifies it as Historic.
tldr.outcome: The memo says RFC 3525 may introduce the protocol but is misleading as a description of its current standardization or deployment.

today: RFC 5125 is Informational and obsoletes RFC 3525 by reclassifying it as Historic. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 5125.

sections.title: The Protocol After RFC 3525
sections.content:
The Gateway Control Protocol Version 1 in RFC 3525 was developed jointly by the IETF Megaco Working Group and ITU-T Study Group 16. The ITU-T published the same contents as Recommendation H.248.1, originally called H.248.

The RFC says the ITU-T later took ownership of the protocol and continued to develop it. Corrections and clarifications were incorporated into later H.248.1 versions and an implementors' guide.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF and ITU-T developed the protocol together. The ITU-T later continued its development as H.248.1.

sections.title: Why RFC 3525 Became Historic
sections.content:
RFC 5125 reports that H.248.1 version 1 was republished with agreed changes and that later versions followed. It describes version 2 as the version most widely deployed at the time of RFC 5125 and says version 3 had also been published.

The memo concludes that RFC 3525 can serve as an introduction to Megaco/H.248 but is misleading as a description of the protocol as then standardized or deployed. It therefore reclassifies RFC 3525 as Historic.
sections.plainLanguage: By the time of this memo, the protocol had newer published versions. The old RFC could still introduce the topic, but it no longer accurately described the protocol's then-current state.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
The memo requires no new IANA action. Registries established by RFC 3525 and extended by successive H.248.1 versions remain in force, including the requirement for expert review by an IESG-designated expert.

Reclassifying RFC 3525 has no security implications, according to the memo.
sections.plainLanguage: The existing registries and their expert-review requirement remain in force. The memo says the reclassification has no security implications.
